explanations.explanation: That's the job, friend. The LORD tells Moses and Eleazar, "Take a census of the whole congregation of Israel by the houses of their fathers…" (Numbers 26:2). A census is a count, and this one is organized by the houses of their fathers. I think whoever had to keep track of all those names had a long day coming. Me? I'd lose count at the second tribe and start over.

No altar in this passage, friend. The LORD's order is about counting people, not building anything. He says, "Take a census of the whole congregation of Israel by the houses of their fathers…" (Numbers 26:2). Save the hammer and nails for another day.

Good guess, but nobody is picking judges here. The LORD tells Moses and Eleazar to take a census, a count of the congregation by the houses of their fathers (Numbers 26:2). It's a list of names and numbers, not a list of leaders. Nobody gets a robe in this one.
Yes, army. The LORD says to count those "…twenty years of age or older who can serve in the army of Israel." (Numbers 26:2). So the count has an age line and a job line. It's not a list of everybody.

Close to the right kind of idea, but not the word. The text says "army," not council (Numbers 26:2). I think a council would've meant a lot more sitting down. This count was about those twenty or older who could serve in the army of Israel.

I get it, fields sounds peaceful. But the LORD says to count those who "…can serve in the army of Israel." (Numbers 26:2). The line the text draws is age and army service, not a man's daily work. So the word that fits the blank is army, not fields. Nice try, friend, and I'd still take a field over a drill any day.

That's it, friend. The LORD says, "Increase the inheritance for a large tribe and decrease it for a small one; each tribe is to receive its inheritance according to the number of those registered." (Numbers 26:54). So the count wasn't just for show. The numbers decided how big the share would be.

explanations.answer: The order the sons were born
explanations.explanation: Birth order sounds fair, but it's not what the LORD says. He ties each share to the number registered: "each tribe is to receive its inheritance according to the number of those registered." (Numbers 26:54). A big tribe gets more and a small tribe gets less. Being the oldest brother's tribe doesn't change the math.

Nice try, but camp spots never come up here. The LORD says the land is divided "…according to the number of names." (Numbers 26:53). Sitting closer to the front gets you nothing. It's all about the count.
Lot is right. The LORD says, "Indeed, the land must be divided by lot…" (Numbers 26:55). A lot is a way of choosing, a bit like drawing straws. Nobody gets to say "I want the spot by the river."

A vote sounds fair, but that's not the word. The LORD says the land "…must be divided by lot…" (Numbers 26:55). A vote would mean campaigning, and I think that would've taken forever. A lot settles it.

Age is a fun guess, but the text doesn't say it. The LORD says, "Each inheritance is to be divided by lot among the larger and smaller tribes." (Numbers 26:56). Big tribe or small tribe, the word is lot. Before that, He says to "Increase the inheritance for a large tribe and decrease it for a small one…" (Numbers 26:54). So the size comes from the number registered, and the lot is how it gets divided.

True, friend, and here's the reason the text gives. The Levites "…were not numbered among the other Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites." (Numbers 26:62). They got their own count: 23,000, every male a month old or more. Same census, separate list. I like a clean answer, and you gave me one.

Ooh, so close, but this one is true, friend. The text says the Levites "…were not numbered among the other Israelites, because no inheritance was given to them among the Israelites." (Numbers 26:62). So they weren't left out. They had their own count of 23,000, every male a month old or more. Think of it as a second list instead of a missing one.

Not quite, friend. The text says, "Among all these, however, there was not one who had been numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest when they counted the Israelites in the Wilderness of Sinai." (Numbers 26:64). So it wasn't most of them. It was none of them, apart from two.

Right, it's false. "Among all these, however, there was not one who had been numbered by Moses and Aaron the priest when they counted the Israelites in the Wilderness of Sinai." (Numbers 26:64). Not most, but not one. Whoa, that's a whole new crowd.

Yes, die. "For the LORD had told them that they would surely die in the wilderness." (Numbers 26:65). It's a heavy line, and the text says it plainly. That's why nobody from the Sinai count shows up in this new one, except two. Those two are Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

Rest sounds gentle, but that's not the word. The text says the LORD "…had told them that they would surely die in the wilderness." (Numbers 26:65). It's a heavy one, friend. I think that's why the Sinai names are missing from this count.

Settle is a nice word, but it's not the one in the text. The LORD "…had told them that they would surely die in the wilderness." (Numbers 26:65). That's a heavy line, friend. The text then says the only two left from the Sinai count were Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. The word that fits the blank is die.
Yes, Caleb and Joshua. "Not one was left except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun." (Numbers 26:65). Two names out of a whole crowd. That's quite a short list of survivors.

Not them, friend. Dathan and Abiram, men of Reuben's tribe, rebelled against Moses and Aaron, and "…the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them…" (Numbers 26:9-10). The two left from the Sinai count were "…Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun." (Numbers 26:65).

Not these two. Nadab and Abihu, Aaron's sons, "…died when they offered unauthorized fire before the LORD." (Numbers 26:61). The only two left from the Sinai count were "…Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun." (Numbers 26:65). It's an easy mix-up, since the passage gives us a lot of names.
